findings.title: Nil dereference when TopicUser record does not exist on unsubscribe
findings.body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` if the user has never visited or interacted with the topic (for example, if they were mentioned or invited in a topic they haven't opened yet, or received a mailing list notification before a `TopicUser` row existed). Accessing `tu.notification_level` on line 107 will then raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass`. In addition, directly mutating and saving `tu` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which sets `notifications_changed_at`, `notifications_reason_id`, creates the row if missing, and publishes the change on MessageBus.

findings.title: Visiting the unsubscribe URL twice in a row mutes the topic instead of being idempotent
findings.body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, if the user's notification level is `watching` or `tracking` (`> regular`), the first GET request lowers it to `regular`. If the user reloads the page, clicks the email link a second time, or if an email client / link scanner prefetches the GET URL before the user clicks it, the second GET sees `notification_level == regular` and takes the `else` branch, setting the level to `muted`. Moreover, when the user is already at `regular` (e.g. they received an email because they were `@mentioned` or quoted), unsubscribing mutes the topic, whereas when they were `watching` it only drops them to `regular` (where they will still receive `@mention`/reply emails despite the page saying "You will stop receiving notifications"). A GET unsubscribe endpoint should be idempotent and have consistent semantics.
